svg.title: A nurse is assessing a client who is 2 days post-operative following creation of an ILEOSTOMY. Which assessment finding requires IMMEDIATE notification of the healthcare provider?
svg.desc: A DUSKY stoma suggests ischemia or necrosis — the blood supply is failing — and 8 hours with almost no output from an ileostomy (which should drain liquid stool steadily) suggests obstruction. Together that’s an emergency. A moist pink stoma is normal; serosanguineous (yellow, blood-tinged) drainage is expected post-op — purulent drainage would signal infection. Liquid stool from an ileostomy is exactly what you expect, since it is proximal in the GI tract. Slight peristomal redness is worth watching, not an urgent call. Dr. Meyer’s test-taking trick for “notify the provider” items: picture calling at 3 AM — which finding earns a “thank you, I’ll be right there” instead of “that could have waited until morning”?
